open_points.subject: module-wide installation state
open_points.text: “keep the returned Installation for the life of the process” and functions refer to “the Installation loaded at start”
open_points.question: What must current_token_list, manifest_source, resolve_service_credential, and selected_instance_name do if called before load_installation?
options: Raise a specified initialization error
Raise an existing exception such as RuntimeError
Return None where the return type permits it
Use implicit initialization
open_points.default_guess: Raise RuntimeError for functions that require loaded state, while current_token_list returns None.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: “MUST call read_configuration once at start, keep the returned Installation for the life of the process”
open_points.question: May load_installation be called more than once, and if so does a later successful call replace the process-wide installation or return the first one?
options: Reject or ignore every later call
Return the first installation without rereading
Reload and replace all kept state
open_points.default_guess: Treat the first successful call as initialization and return the kept installation on later calls.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: “a failed check propagates InstallationRejectedError and nothing is kept”
open_points.question: If a later load_installation call is permitted and fails after an installation is already kept, does “nothing is kept” clear the old state or only mean the failed candidate is not kept?
options: Clear all old state
Preserve the previously loaded state
Later calls are forbidden, so this case cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Preserve previously loaded state.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: “MUST call read_configuration once at start ... and keep the SHA-256 of the file's bytes as the last read digest”
open_points.question: How can load_installation obtain the digest of the exact bytes validated by read_configuration when read_configuration returns only Installation and reopening the path may yield different bytes?
options: Have read_configuration save its read bytes or digest as hidden module state
Open and hash the path again after read_configuration
Perform an additional internal read and accept the race
Change an internal helper so both functions share one read result
open_points.default_guess: Use a private read helper returning both Installation and digest, with read_configuration exposing only the Installation.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes, opening config_path as read_configuration does”
open_points.question: Which config_path does the zero-argument current_token_list use?
options: The exact string passed to the first successful load_installation
A normalized absolute path captured at load time
The path from the most recent successful load_installation
open_points.default_guess: Use an absolute path resolved and captured by the first successful load_installation.

open_points.subject: configuration path handling
open_points.text: “opening config_path ... component by component”
open_points.question: For a relative config_path, is it resolved against the current working directory on every access or against the directory in effect when load_installation was called?
options: Resolve anew against the current working directory
Capture an absolute path at load time
Reject relative paths
open_points.default_guess: Capture an absolute path at load time.

open_points.subject: safe component-by-component opening
open_points.text: “component by component without following a symbolic link at any component”
open_points.question: What are the required semantics for empty paths, '.', '..', repeated separators, a symlinked starting directory, and platforms without equivalent no-follow open operations?
options: Normalize dot components before traversal
Traverse dot and parent components literally while rejecting symlinks
Reject paths containing '.' or '..'
Support only platforms providing secure descriptor-relative traversal
open_points.default_guess: Use descriptor-relative traversal from the appropriate root or current directory, permit dot and parent components, and apply no-follow to every opened non-dot component.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “opening config_path as read_configuration does, component by component without following a symbolic link at any component” versus “applies exactly four checks”
open_points.question: Does token refresh repeat read_configuration's regular-file, owner, and permission checks, or does “as read_configuration does” refer only to symlink-safe traversal?
options: Repeat all file-security checks
Only enforce no-symlink traversal and readability
Repeat the checks only when the digest changes
open_points.default_guess: Treat the phrase as requiring only no-symlink traversal, because the four refresh checks are stated as exhaustive.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file”
open_points.question: Must every changed or initially unreadable file cause a second independent open/read, and which read determines the digest and token contents if the file changes between the two reads?
options: Always perform a second read and use only its bytes
Reuse the first successful read and call validation of those bytes the re-read
Retry only after an initial read failure
open_points.default_guess: Always perform the specified second read and use its bytes for both the new digest and token validation.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file” and “when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared”
open_points.question: If the initial read fails but the required re-read succeeds, should the successful re-read install tokens and a digest, or must the initial failure still clear the state?
options: Use the successful re-read normally
Treat any initial failure as final and clear state
Do not retry despite the re-read wording
open_points.default_guess: Use the successful re-read normally; clear the digest only if the re-read also fails.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types” and “a re-read takes only the token list”
open_points.question: During refresh, must the object contain exactly only owner_token and agent_tokens, exactly all Installation fields, or merely valid token members while all other members are ignored?
options: Require only the two token members and reject extras
Require a complete valid Installation object
Require valid token members and ignore all other members
open_points.default_guess: Require valid owner_token and agent_tokens and ignore all other members.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: “it never raises for a bad file”
open_points.question: Which exceptions count as a bad file and must be converted to None, as opposed to programming, resource, or platform errors that may propagate?
options: Catch only expected open, read, JSON, and validation failures
Catch every Exception
Catch all BaseException values
open_points.default_guess: Catch expected filesystem, decoding, JSON, and data-validation exceptions only.

open_points.subject: current_token_list and load_installation
open_points.text: “last read digest,” “kept list,” and “keep the returned Installation for the life of the process”
open_points.question: What atomicity and ordering are required when load_installation and current_token_list are called concurrently from multiple threads?
options: Serialize all access with a lock
Allow races and last writer wins
Require callers to serialize access
open_points.default_guess: Serialize reads and updates of the module state with a lock.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “the bytes ... parse as one JSON object”
open_points.question: Which JSON encodings and byte-order marks are accepted: UTF-8 only, or every encoding permitted or auto-detected by the chosen JSON parser?
options: Strict UTF-8 without BOM
UTF-8 with an optional BOM
JSON's UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 encodings
open_points.default_guess: Accept the encodings handled by the standard-library JSON byte parser.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation”
open_points.question: Are duplicate textual object member names invalid, or may the JSON parser collapse them so the last value wins?
options: Reject every duplicate object member at every nesting level
Reject duplicates only in the top-level object
Allow the parser's last-value-wins behavior
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate object member names at every level.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types”
open_points.question: Must JSON values already have the exact declared primitive and collection types, or may the imported model's validation coerce values such as arrays to tuples or non-strings to strings?
options: Perform strict primitive validation but map JSON arrays to tuple fields
Use the imported models' normal validation and coercion
Require literal tuple types, making ordinary JSON arrays invalid
open_points.default_guess: Require exact JSON primitive types and arrays for tuple-valued fields, then construct tuples without other coercion.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long”
open_points.question: Is token length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes, grapheme clusters, or another unit?
options: Python string code points
UTF-8 byte length
User-perceived grapheme clusters
open_points.default_guess: Measure Python string length in Unicode code points.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “grants any permission to group or others”
open_points.question: Does this prohibit only Unix group/other mode bits, or also ACL entries and other platform-specific grants not represented by those bits?
options: Check only group/other mode bits
Check mode bits and access-control lists
Reject files where complete effective access cannot be proven private
open_points.default_guess: Check the Unix group/other permission bits only.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials”
open_points.question: If both collections contain duplicates, which collection's failure must be reported first?
options: Check service_instances first
Check service_credentials first
Use one shared duplicate-check failure without distinguishing the collection
open_points.default_guess: Check service_instances first, then service_credentials.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: “config_path cannot be opened ... the file so opened is not a regular file ...; the bytes cannot be read”
open_points.question: How should failures of descriptor metadata operations, directory traversal, final-component opening, and reads after a successful open be classified among the named checks?
options: Traversal and open failures are the open check; metadata-call failures are their associated metadata checks; read failures are the read check
Classify every filesystem operation failure as cannot be opened
Expose the underlying operating-system exception
open_points.default_guess: Classify traversal/final-open errors as open failures, metadata errors at the relevant metadata check, and byte-read errors as read failures.

open_points.subject: InstallationRejectedError
open_points.text: “MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check” and “class InstallationRejectedError(Exception): pass”
open_points.question: What exact message or structured data names each check, and must offending paths, fields, or service identifiers be included?
options: A specified stable message string for each check
Free-form messages that mention the check
Add structured attributes despite the declared pass-only exception surface
open_points.default_guess: Use concise free-form exception messages with no extra attributes and no sensitive values.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: “MUST find the service_credentials entry of service_id”
open_points.question: What error is raised if no Installation has been loaded, as distinct from an installation with no credential configured for that service?
options: CredentialUnresolvedError treating it as not configured
RuntimeError for uninitialized module state
InstallationRejectedError
open_points.default_guess: Raise RuntimeError for uninitialized module state.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: “missing, unreadable, not private, larger than ... or not valid UTF-8, or its value is empty or holds a control character”
open_points.question: What is the exact check order, and which reason covers a symlink, non-regular file, wrong owner, unsafe mode, or metadata-operation failure?
options: Use the listed order and classify symlink/non-regular/owner/mode failures as not private
Check file kind, ownership, mode, size, read, decoding, empty, then controls with distinct reasons
Classify symlink and non-regular files as unreadable, and ownership/mode as not private
open_points.default_guess: Classify missing separately; symlink, non-regular, metadata, and open/read failures as unreadable; ownership or unsafe mode as not private; then check size, UTF-8, empty, and controls.

open_points.subject: CredentialUnresolvedError
open_points.text: “whose reason names the service and the failing check” and “class CredentialUnresolvedError(Exception): pass”
open_points.question: Is the reason only the exception message or a required attribute, and what exact stable format must it use?
options: Use only Exception.args with a free-form message
Define a reason attribute and a service_id attribute
Use a specified message template
open_points.default_guess: Use only a concise message in Exception.args containing service_id and the check name.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: “decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present”
open_points.question: What counts as one newline: LF only, a CRLF pair, lone CR, or any Unicode line-break sequence?
options: Remove one trailing LF byte only
Remove one trailing LF and a preceding CR as one CRLF newline
Remove one trailing Unicode line-break sequence
open_points.default_guess: Remove one trailing LF character only, leaving a preceding CR to be rejected as a control character.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: “its value ... holds a control character”
open_points.question: Which characters are controls: ASCII C0 only, C0 plus DEL, C0/C1, or every Unicode character in general category Cc?
options: ASCII U+0000 through U+001F
ASCII C0 plus U+007F
Unicode general category Cc, including C0, DEL, and C1
open_points.default_guess: Reject every Unicode character in general category Cc.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: “the value is the file's content decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present” and “its value is empty or holds a control character”
open_points.question: Are emptiness and control-character checks applied before or after removing the trailing newline?
options: After newline removal
Before newline removal
Empty after removal but controls before removal
open_points.default_guess: Apply both checks after removing the trailing newline.

open_points.subject: manifest_source
open_points.text: “MUST return ManifestSource with manifest_location and manifest_revision of the Installation loaded at start”
open_points.question: Must each call construct a new ManifestSource or return one cached instance?
options: Construct a new equal value on every call
Cache and return the same instance
open_points.default_guess: Construct a new ManifestSource on every call.
